chapter: Rhythm Club, studio dates and the 1930s big bands
title: Head-arranged "Broadway" with Dakota Staton
summary: On a Late Late Show date, McRae and a team of top players put together "Broadway" for Dakota Staton without any written arrangement.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: When we were recording the Late Late Show, we did a thing with Dakota Staton. Dave Cavahaugh is sitting in the control booth. He say, "Teddy, you got it."

I say, "Okay." So I walked over to Hinton -- you know, who was on that date -- all these top guys on this date -- join all these fellows.
We all worked together. And we put together "Broadway" -- talked it over what they were going to do.
And they hit the introduction and Dakota Staton come in singing "Broadway." All that's head (inaudible) arrangements. All with (inaudible) head arrangements, just like that.
They all had arrangements. No music. I hand them all piano copies (inaudible). Hinton a bass copy You don't hear no piano with a bass (inaudible). All knew it.
They put (inaudible). I say, "Dave, (inaudible) put that on music, huh?"
What if you just could write that head down? A million dollar (inaudible) arrangement!
When we went into record, we didn't use no -- we had all these all star guys walk in the studio. We put together arrangements so quick,

it make your eyes jump out, you know. I say, "Yall ready?" "Yeah, we ready." "Let's go. Let's make it." And the first time down they would make it. If they want to make another one, they wouldn't have to -- the guy say, "That's good enough, you don't have to make no more. Go to the next one." Because we would put it together. Like we worked -- you know, like the guys were so good working together. You know, these are all top musicians. They could feel each other. We could get together on a little thing and say, "Hey, let's do an arrangement, let's do "Dinah." Guy (Inaudible) make the introduction -- boom.
